incidents.summary: D1: binary attachments and unlisted endpoint runtimes were admitted without a bound for the complete request.
incidents.expected: Refuse before the first generation, retain the measured parts and executable route or probe steps, and admit only documented binary bounds or capacity evidence under the same key with output room reserved.

incidents.summary: A rare packet branch, transport change or unsupported coverage claim could escape fixture-only checks.
incidents.expected: Source inventories reject undeclared writes and calls; matrix coverage requires passing executed evidence and preserves required stops.

incidents.summary: A size stop could register a new route without moving its existing review head, or omit a task-kind outcome.
incidents.expected: The guard retains all size-kind rows, rejects route-only stop endings and executes C9/C12 paths to recorded review results.

incidents.summary: The legacy result-parts v1 fixture inherited the v3 source rules introduced in 0.89.1, so its refresh correctly retained the invoked v3 session instead of entering parts v2.
incidents.expected: Construct only the historical v1 series under its original v2 source rules. Restore the current v3 default before refreshing changed evidence into a new parts-v2 series, and authenticate all stored v1 turns with unchanged packet, prompt and request bytes.

incidents.summary: The keyed capacity classifier introduced a list of runtime and configuration metadata triples that the output-view registry scanner mistook for stored record changes.
incidents.expected: Keep the classification table in an immutable tuple with identical classification output. The unchanged record-writer scanner finds no writes in the capacity evidence module, and every actual written record kind retains its placement.

incidents.class: review capacity diagnostics and call ordering
incidents.summary: T3 and T4: separate verified routes were serialized without actionable capacity advice, and waiting series needed an outer restart loop.
incidents.expected: Planned waits and queued calls name their store and route limits. A store wait on an idle verified route supplies a scheduler for participating verified routes. Three drivers on one route finish in request order without external commands or automatic stop records.

incidents.summary: The route-capacity snapshot let JSON decoding in its advisory task report replace the existing malformed-packet terminal stop with CLI input_io.
incidents.expected: An unavailable advisory task measure preserves the scientific terminal refusal, series exit code and retained diagnostic.

incidents.summary: A source request could require hundreds of padded full-text delivery turns without a cost stop.
incidents.expected: The session reports pending captures and parts, stops before dispatch above its turn plan or projected input capacity, and names executable compact-capture and preserved-slot repair steps.

incidents.summary: A session paid for each continuation without reporting the measured output profile or expected calls.
incidents.expected: Session forecasts report the matching request-kind over-limit share, output and duration medians where observed, and expected calls without changing effort or reviewer inputs.

incidents.summary: A forming import could add many large artifact bodies without a size report before recording.
incidents.expected: A check measures projected imported records and transitive bodies, tokens, registered limits and turns; recording and replay retain the original import receipt.

incidents.summary: A session continuation did not report its fitted input beside the route limit before another call.
incidents.expected: The continuation and its assignment/status reports expose the fitted request measure, pending parts and projection outside stored packet and request bytes.

incidents.summary: A value account could cite large searches and their captured responses without a size diagnostic.
incidents.expected: A fresh value receipt reports account-record and body characters with shared route measures outside the stored value and receipt; historical replays need no evidence reads.

incidents.summary: Stage 2 plans and refusal replacements met keyed input evidence and scoped stop drivers from release 0.89.2.
incidents.expected: The driver reads explicit scoped kinds and retains its ending; new plans and refusal forms use only their route execution-key witness while output profiles stay separate. V6 admission and forecasts use the same keyed evidence. Every coded ending keeps its selected head and action, including requested stops and startup refusals, with a workspace fallback when snapshots fail. Requested stop_id remains the release identity; series_stop_id and details.receipt identify each distinct retained ending. A selected successor can use authenticated earlier history that is unselected; missing or unverified historical output still blocks dispatch. Inferred smaller parts tasks retain their direct capacity predecessor and the original scientific slot without changing the frozen parent. Parts progress follows the current authenticated replacement allowance instead of inferring exhaustion from two raw refusals.

incidents.class: bounded reading admission, retention and capacity recovery
incidents.summary: The reading chain accumulated receipts and excerpt metadata outside its advertised grants, then its final could not fit after 57 turns.
incidents.expected: V7 binds a stored plan, inventory and reconstructed state; bounded reading requests reach a one-request final with all grants used. Eight floor targets start v7, nine fall back to byte-identical v6, and an unserved packet has executable decision answers. Dense failed-final measurements survive export without compounded margins. Pages use fixed row ids, references authenticate, and a max-effort 138371-token event halves material on the same route.

incidents.summary: New exports repeated unchanged full texts and searches after an earlier chain stopped.
incidents.expected: A stored v7 selection credits unchanged delivered ranges and completed original searches from eligible v5/v6 prefixes. Changed sources affect notes and exclude their entries; later chains do not alter stored selections. First-assignment integration is a separate lane.

incidents.class: reading continuity and bounded carried material
incidents.summary: A new chain repeated unchanged sources while a long earlier chain could not reach its final.
incidents.expected: The first v7 assignment freezes an authenticated selection, credits unchanged ranges and retains entries within serialized grants. Required affected notes precede other material; optional notes have a bounded index, complete pages and passage access. A v6 fallback reports the chains v7 would carry without crediting them.

incidents.summary: The earlier reading chain could not fit its final after reading all required units.
incidents.expected: A v7 final verifies the stored carried selection and every own state, records its finding with origin turns, and becomes stale if an origin no longer authenticates.

incidents.summary: A v7 final returned an earlier decision/objections/reason contract; refused reading and final positions need frozen-notice replacements, while an exhausted or oversized chain needs an admitted successor.
incidents.expected: Replace at the same position and reviewer: reading material pays the notice charge with its floor, while a one-request final retains its material level and uses the stored notice reserve. A reduced-level capacity replacement preserves its material and frozen notice, records the level and actual notice size, and authenticates historically. Planned notices obey route wire bounds; no-plan notices keep their earlier bytes, acceptance and errors. The final frame independently bounds its allowance rows, page and remaining envelope. Record and verify the corrected finding without rewriting history. Exhausted and input-limited chains export only to an admitted v7 or v6 successor, or stop with executable answers while preserving verified history.

incidents.summary: A provider safeguard stop at one reading position ended the chain and repeated completed readings on the next export.
incidents.expected: After the last floor sequence, admit an unresolved final over the authenticated complete unread set; page all ranges and attempts in fixed order, preserve refusal replacements, and carry completed readings into later exports.

incidents.summary: New chains read unchanged full texts again after an earlier chain stopped before its final finding.
incidents.expected: A new v7 chain selects verified unchanged units across v5/v6 origins, delivers only missing or changed ranges and required affected notes, and records a finding whose mixed-chain origins verify without changing the stored selection.

incidents.summary: A v7 reading response body limit retried the same task and stopped before smaller levels, while plain and compacted input limits at reading and final floors restarted the same route through a new export.
incidents.expected: Response limits visit the next smaller pinned reading level on the same route and effort before the floor decision. Input limits retain that size decision and its executable answers at the floor, preserving verified turns; legacy input and v7 denser-ratio successor admissions remain available.

incidents.summary: A refused final with full retained entries placed the unread member and refusal notice in the same reserve.
incidents.expected: Reserve the required unread core in the final frame, then charge rows and pending pages only against free material room and the reserve left by the wire notice; retain and authenticate the complete unread set.

incidents.summary: The reviewed 0.90.0 texts removed a protocol label that G2 asserted and changed certified source ASTs; a new prompt lookup dictionary also introduced an undeclared literal key.
incidents.expected: G2 checks that the accepted export warns that both resolved outcomes are blocked and only an unresolved finding can be recorded, with the same refusal code and forecast. Refresh source certificates only after reviewing their text changes. A changed declaration remains reported until it has its own declaration review.

incidents.summary: G12 still expected an identical rerun of a refused first native assignment after D2 introduced the exhausted-position handoff for native assignments that cannot carry a refusal replacement.
incidents.expected: Keep the openness.finding refusal with code openness_finding_invalid when searches change, and hand off the first native assignment to export with review_slot_exhausted and outcome scientific_refused. A valid resolved answer over changed records instead hands off with openness_packet_outdated, while a valid unresolved answer remains recordable.

incidents.summary: A refused final output was retried without its contract diagnosis or the delivered part-relative offsets.
incidents.expected: The planner executes an authenticated replacement carrying the current refusal, bounded to its route, and reaches a recorded review or the exhausted role handoff. Validator upgrades retain successor finality and every stored request, observation and refusal.

incidents.summary: Synthetic binary backends escaped integration helpers; nested setup failures then left claim modules, Codex runtime declarations and historical openness protocols patched. Reviewer subprocesses also lost the fixture import path.
incidents.expected: Review helpers scope backend patches, nested fixtures clean up even after setup fails, and reviewer children import their fixture dependencies without inherited PYTHONPATH.

incidents.summary: Archived synthetic routes lacked the newly explicit fixture runtime capacity contract, and a source-rule comparison unintentionally entered multipart review under the default output profile.
incidents.expected: Historical synthetic executors declare keyed capacity without rewriting stored bytes, and ordinary source-rule comparisons declare their synthetic single-output profile.

incidents.summary: The legacy slate byte-preservation test and the large streamed publication fixture recorded requests that their synthetic routes could not cover under the admission introduced in 0.89.2.
incidents.expected: Only the pre-0.89.2 legacy assignment is built without the later admission; new slates use current admission, and large streamed publications retain files above 1 MiB and two ready manuscript reviews using keyed capacity evidence restored by class cleanup.

incidents.class: release merge compatibility and synthetic fixture drift
incidents.summary: PR 143 exposed revisionless legacy assignment selection, omitted capacity parameters in staged estimates, stale synthetic review inputs, and an admission race that hid a missing assignment binding. Nested staged fixture setup could also leak an observation backend after an exception.
incidents.expected: Legacy revisionless assignments retain their admission and later replacements remain selected. Staged estimates retain frame capacity parameters without rewriting packets. Synthetic reviews bind stored attempts and prompts, preserve historical protocol journeys, exhaust permitted refusal replacements before a new repair, and restore nested fixture patches even after setup fails.

incidents.class: release CI contract and fixture drift
incidents.summary: Stage 2 moved snapshot authentication outside status timing, retained stale expectations for new capacity notices, finding and lineage refusals, watched the former provenance derivation function, and combined archived-runtime refusal tests with an available synthetic backend. The incident ledger also retained a renamed test identifier.
incidents.expected: Status timing includes snapshot authentication on healthy and malformed contexts; tests exercise current contracts while replaying stored prompt versions and hashes unchanged, and archived-backend refusal tests explicitly leave that backend unavailable.

incidents.class: v7 reading packet and capacity contract
incidents.summary: Final frames hid the decisive ids required by source_settles.
incidents.expected: The final carries the measured list up to 10000 wire characters; larger lists become requestable fixed fields.

incidents.class: v7 reading packet and capacity contract
incidents.summary: Passage requests rejected logical handles shown by carried entries and final sources.
incidents.expected: Logical handles resolve deterministically to the first delivery part holding the anchor, including through replacements and verification.

incidents.class: v7 reading packet and capacity contract
incidents.summary: Final gap rows hid their meaning behind artifact references.
incidents.expected: Forecast rows state condition, blocked outcomes and target; reviewer text is charged to its target grant and only retained gaps reach the final.

incidents.class: v7 reading packet and capacity contract
incidents.summary: Grouping affected notes by origin hid interior handles and an unseen note required a known phrase.
incidents.expected: Every note has its own bounded index and list row; a null anchor requests its start and charges the passage allowance.

incidents.class: v7 reading packet and capacity contract
incidents.summary: A material response credited reading units while dropping their notes, excerpts and gaps.
incidents.expected: The reading output refuses material with invalid_review_material at /stage and a notice-bearing replacement reads the uncredited units. Arguments continue only between finals; earlier protocols keep their bytes.

incidents.summary: A final after 57 reading turns exceeded the route while the earlier floor forecasts reported room.
incidents.expected: A stored v7 plan bounds every turn, retains authenticated v5 readings without fulltext redelivery, and reaches an authenticated recorded finding.

incidents.summary: The planner exhausts its output-cap attempt allowance at 60000 characters while the stored reading ladder still has levels of 30000 and 15000.
incidents.expected: The planner executes every lower material level at the same route and effort before applying the floor decision.

incidents.summary: A text-only problem reading chain on codex_cli_visual_v1 is rejected as a native visual problem-result assignment before v7 admission. The visual request builder also raises review_visual_input_mismatch for admitted scaled reading packets.
incidents.expected: On 0.91.0 a visual v7 reading stops before any request and its declared decision registers and probes a text route of the same model, then exports, checks and records a first assignment there. Native visual text turns belong to the 0.93.0 transport release.

incidents.summary: A refused final at a non-floor level loses earlier note fill when its notice is subtracted from material instead of charged to the plan reserve.
incidents.expected: Ruling 39 keeps all six final material fields at the same level, charges the notice to its reserve, and reaches a recorded finding without changing earlier records.

incidents.summary: A newly recorded material search makes a v7 packet stale after its first reading, but the planner still continues the old native packet.
incidents.expected: The v7 planner gives the export handoff, the new chain inherits the measured ratio and verified ranges, and the successor records its finding.

incidents.summary: The unread-final replacement lookup read all assignment membership and invalidated an ordinary bar preparation after an unrelated assignment was added.
incidents.expected: Bind only assignments whose context.unread.assignment_id names the origin; unrelated assignments preserve preparation and a newly inserted successor for that origin invalidates it.

incidents.summary: The 0.91.0 integration omitted carried/successor source declarations and retained certificates from before v7 dispatch; the concurrent guard schema also predated the final gap and affected-note shapes.
incidents.expected: Declare both source modules, retain the closed current v7 shapes and both v6/v7 evidence sets, and review source and call differences before certifying them.

incidents.summary: The merged series guard retained the call inventory and entry membership expectations from before v7 refusal-turn integration.
incidents.expected: Pin the position-context reader used by series diagnostics and combine the original entry evidence with its separately reviewed capture-interval addition; all entry refusals keep their executable decision.

incidents.summary: The activation of the order (v7, v6) in 0.91.0 made the single-turn branch of prepare_packet refuse every openness packet, so a math-solver openness review that fits one input became a reading chain.
incidents.expected: A math openness packet that one input of its route holds stays one native turn under exactory-openness-reading-math-v1; a new problem openness review starts a chain under the first protocol of the order whose admission accepts it.

incidents.summary: A class decorator patched the order of new problem chains for the v6 guard tests and restored it when a test method returned; the cleanup of a nested openness case ran after that and wrote (v6,) back, so the later tests of the same CI shard ran under (v6,).
incidents.expected: The v6 guard tests start their patch of the order in setUp with the first cleanup, so the released order (v7, v6) is restored after the cleanups of every nested case.

incidents.summary: Three tests still assumed what 0.91.0 replaced: the supplied reading journey matched the v6 prompt sentence in a chain that now starts under v7, the closing test of the series code groups admitted only the groups stored_state and named_cause, and the alternate representation test expected a v6 single turn.
incidents.expected: The supplied journey pins its chain to v6 and a v7 journey delivers the reported origin and records the finding; a group with its own next step admits only its declared conditions; a v7 chain reads only the selected representation, and a v6 packet keeps its single turn.

incidents.summary: Accounts read a work year and reading revision that production never writes.
incidents.expected: Command-written readings date facts by reliable arXiv version assertions and remain unordered in gain history.

incidents.class: review start visibility and bounded render takeover
incidents.summary: A running reviewer call had a committed invocation while series.json still showed no run. Concurrent renders and failed claimed passes also need durable catch-up and accurate failure advisories.
incidents.expected: A new call requests a zero-wait render before transport, with at most two lock attempts and two passes including failure recording. Busy or failed renders preserve the call, retain work and failure details, and the next successful lock-holding render consumes the retained marker.

incidents.class: explicit whole-store optimistic revision check during reviewer completion
incidents.summary: T7: a foreground problem-value expected revision 698 while a review route probe completed at 699. The measurement retained stale_revision without retrying.
incidents.expected: Reviewer completion between the foreground revision read and preparation or commit refuses stale_revision without a value or request receipt. The registry says to continue and the message says to read the current revision; retrying the same payload and request ID at that revision succeeds and replays without another mutation. This is the documented whole-store optimistic check, not a change to revision protection.

incidents.summary: The admission of the next export upgraded the version 1 minimum of a v5 packet to version 2 and kept the evidence of the old packet. Where a bound search names a reading, the upgraded minimum binds that reading as a supporting reading, the projected packet did not carry it, and the stopped chain ended with openness_reading_incomplete in place of the handoff export.
incidents.expected: The projected packet carries every record that its minimum binds, built by the function that the export uses, and a chain of v5 or v6 whose next request cannot fit ends with the handoff export when a protocol admits the projected packet.

incidents.class: refusal replacement across a route renewal
incidents.summary: A refused turn whose route record pins an earlier reviewer runtime got its replacement on that record. The call ended with review_route_runtime_stale, the assignment stayed as the head of the position, and review-assignment refused the same replacement on a new route record with the same adapter, model, endpoint and configuration. On the store of record 7 at revision 200 the series of bar B ended with the handoff review-route and no reviewer call.
incidents.expected: No command records an assignment on a route record that pins another reviewer runtime. The plan of a refused session turn on such a record is the replacement on a verified route record of the same identity with the installed runtime, or the handoff that names what such a record lacks, or the step of the role when no such record can carry the replacement, each before any assignment is recorded. The replacement keeps the reviewer, the slot and the position, its notice lists every refusal of the position, and its origin verifies from stored records.

incidents.summary: An accepted output correction was authenticated against the installed reviewer runtime. After an update of the reviewer CLI or of a transport module, after a change of the program path, or without the reviewer program, the correction was not selected and its assignment showed review_output_refused. A correction call on a stale route record, or on a route whose reviewer program was not installed, recorded a failed correction without an answer and used the one correction of the assignment.
incidents.expected: A correction authenticates against the runtime that its route record pins, when its call finishes and at every later read, whatever runtime is installed. A correction that records another runtime than the pinned one is not selected. A correction call is refused before any record, and the correction stays available, when the route record is stale and when the reviewer program of a Codex or a Claude route is not installed.

incidents.summary: An accepted output correction was admitted again at every read, on the records of that time. A record that was written after it took its selection away: a retirement of the route of the assignment or of the correction, a later probe that did not verify, a contamination event, a later contamination in the lineage of the repair, or a later assignment in the slot. The assignment then showed review_output_refused with no output; the refusal planner planned, and the harness recorded, a refusal replacement that discarded the accepted correction; a context repair that followed carried the refused raw outputs in place of the corrected output; and a record that arrived during the correction call turned its answer into an invalid correction.
incidents.expected: A correction is authenticated against the review records as they stood before its invocation was recorded, when its call finishes and at every later read. A later record leaves it selected and acts in the state of the assignment as it acts on an accepted attempt: no obligation after a retirement of either route that names no assignment in the exposure lineage of the repair, the context obligation after a probe that does not verify or after a contamination, review_context_repair_stale after a later cause event of the repair (a contamination or a retirement that names an assignment in that lineage), and review_assignment_replaced after a successor, which takes the corrected output as its history. A new correction call keeps every condition on the records of today.

incidents.class: rebuild of the payload of a started call
incidents.summary: record-check rebuilt the payload of each committed route probe from id and route_id only. A capacity probe, which holds the optional member capacity since 0.89.2, then failed the payload binding of its capture, and record-check of a copy of a live record stopped at authentication with review_invocation_unverified. Five of the 34 captures of that record failed this binding. The step that review-stop gave for a captured capacity probe also lacked capacity, and the store refused a replay of that step with request_id_conflict.
incidents.expected: Each kind of owned call defines its required and optional payload members once, in the module that starts the call. The start check and every rebuild of the payload of a started call read that definition: record-check, the step of a captured call in review-stop, the step of a staged dispatch, the resume plan of a head and the staged task run that resumes a recorded dispatch. Each rebuild gives back the payload of the start, with every optional member that the start received. record-check of the copy of that record is ready, and the step of a captured capacity probe finishes the probe without a reviewer call.

incidents.class: refusal notice of an evidence array
incidents.summary: A study bar reviewer wrote the artifact member of a packet evidence entry and the citation of a prior_context passage as evidence entries. The check evidence.shape stopped at the first refused entry and gave only the path of the array and its message, and the notice of each replacement had empty details. The prompt of a study review states no form of an evidence entry, so the two replacements returned refused forms again: 45 of 45, 45 of 45 and 15 of 15 entries of every evidence array were refused, and the slot position ended without a bar. The path of a refusal also did not name the array in two places: the evidence of a reassessment finding was refused under the path /reassessment or under no path, and the evidence of an adjudication under no path.
incidents.expected: The check evidence.shape checks every entry of the array and raises the code and the message of the first refused entry. Its details add refused_indexes (the positions of the refused entries in the array of the answer, at most 100), refused_count and notice, the accepted forms of an evidence entry, in the form of record reference that the call accepts. An array of the three forms that is refused as a whole gets notice alone, and an array of another grammar gets the positions of its refused entries and never notice. Every caller of the three forms names its array in path, the notice of a replacement shows the three details, and a stored refusal or replacement keeps its details and stays verified.

incidents.summary: A probe whose program exited with status 0 was recorded as failed, with the observation "Probe output capture failed: stale_revision" and no outputs, while the capture of a second probe committed its records. Each write of a capture was a compare-and-swap on the revision of the whole store, with 8 attempts within 8 seconds, and one attempt took about 4 seconds on a store of the study's size. A refusal while an output was pinned became the recorded outcome, and a probe id cannot be recorded again. Probes that were launched together were refused with stale_revision or store_busy before their programs ran.
incidents.expected: The records that the launcher and the worker write for a probe commit against the records that their preparation read, and each waits up to 600 seconds for a busy store. A refusal of the store or of the artifact store during a capture is raised and is not recorded as an outcome. The message of a store refusal after the wait says what the same command with the same id does next, and after the launch that command records the outcome from the kept files. Probes whose launches or captures meet are each recorded with the exit status of the program and every output. An outcome file that an earlier worker wrote for stale_revision or store_busy is captured again. A failed read of an output records capture_failure with the exit status of the program.

incidents.class: completion of the step of a series ending
incidents.summary: Since 0.90.0 the ending of review-series completed the step of the ending and then copied it over every step of every answer that had the same command. For the stop review_turn_failures_exhausted of a bar, the answer "Keep this route" then began with the review-context event of kind route_retired, which is the first step of the answer "Move to another route". For the stop review_pending_delivery_over_plan, every select-main-capture step named the first pending source: in the two stored endings of a bar slot of the record, seven capture steps named one version, and six of the seven pending sources were named by no step.
incidents.expected: The ending replaces a step of an answer by the completed step of the ending only when that step is the step of the ending. Every other step keeps its own id, payload, chooses and prerequisites and still receives the arguments of its command. For every stop whose plan builds a decision, the answers of the ending hold the id, command and payload of each step that the plan built. The identity of an ending and the stored stops do not change.

incidents.summary: A record that finishes paid work was a compare-and-swap on the revision of the whole store, tried again for 8 seconds, while one write takes 4 to 48 seconds on a store of a study's size. Another command that wrote, or only read, refused it. exactory-lab run spent an admission before its program started, or ended refused after its program; a remote step kept an unknown outcome although the service had answered; an acquisition ended without the responses of its requests, a cohort collection without a page, and a direct deposit or the concept DOI of a version draft without its record.
incidents.expected: The records of an admitted run, of a remote intent, of an acquisition, of a cohort page, of a full-text job, of a direct deposit and of the concept DOI of a version draft commit against the records that they read, or at the revision that the write lock finds, and wait for a busy store for at most 600 seconds; within that wait a COMMIT that readers hold up keeps its transaction. A refusal after the wait is store_busy with a message that says what is kept and which command goes on, and the refusal of an answer of a remote step carries only the members that the step needs. The same exactory-lab run command starts a claimed local run whose program never started.

incidents.summary: The record that releases a Colab job was a compare-and-swap on the revision of the whole store with one attempt, and the launcher compared two revision reads before it wrote the signal of the runner. A commit of another command in between ended exactory-lab run before the runner started the program; the same command then released the job and was refused until the runner had finished.
incidents.expected: The release commits against the records of the admission check and waits for a busy store for at most 600 seconds; its signal follows the commit; a release found without its signal is checked on a guarded read. A refusal after the wait is store_busy with a message that names the command that goes on.

incidents.summary: The records before a reviewer program starts (the process that starts the program, and the claim, the ready record, the authorization and the start of the worker of a staged task) were tried for 8 seconds or once. A store that another command locked, or that the launching command itself read, ended the worker or the guardian before the reviewer program started, and an attempt of the task or of the turn was spent. The guardian wrote its record inside the time limit of the transport: on a store of 1,004 MB that record took 28 seconds, longer than the 15 seconds of the version check of a Codex route, so no Codex call started.
incidents.expected: The owner of a call records the process that starts a reviewer program before the transport starts its time limit, and a refused record of that process ends the call before the program, past the transport. The five records wait for a locked store for at most 600 seconds, and the launch handshake waits as long. A refusal after the wait is store_busy with a message that says that no reviewer program started; the worker of a staged task writes it to its log or captures it as its failed observation.

incidents.summary: The refusal record of a reviewer output that fails its contract was a compare-and-swap on the revision of the whole store with one attempt, and its failure was swallowed. After a commit of another command the run returned without output_refusal, the plan moved to the next turn on the refused answer, and the second run and the replacement that carries the refusal were refused.
incidents.expected: The refusal record commits against the records that the check of the output read, and it and the read of the store after the run wait for a busy store for at most 600 seconds. A refusal after the wait refuses the command with store_busy and a message that names the request that records the refusal, and review-series runs that request again by itself.

incidents.summary: A command that repeated a committed request ran a write transaction that changed nothing. Its start waited for every writer and its COMMIT for every reader, so on a store of a study's size the repeat was refused with store_busy. Opening a store for creation had the same two waits. With the commit retry of the finishing writes, a read of another command that started while a COMMIT waited was refused after one second, also the first read of a command. The first write of an acquisition and the saved intent of a remote operation were refused when another command committed or held a lock.
incidents.expected: A committed request is answered from a read, a write transaction that finds its request committed ends with ROLLBACK, and the open of an existing store for creation takes no write lock. Inside a command a read waits for a COMMIT in progress, and a COMMIT waits for the readers that hold the store, for at most 600 seconds. The admission of an acquisition commits at the revision that the write lock finds, and the saved intent of a remote operation without a revision of the user commits against the saved intents; both wait for a busy store for at most 600 seconds.
